anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: LXX: unless you believe, you will not understand.
Quoted: I did not come to do my will but the will of the one who sent me.
Not my will but the will of the one who sent me.
You do not know the scriptures — possible.

pass_a_gloss: For they did not attempt the perfect itself in faith but in unbelief, not having known the writings which the prophets were announcing. For unless you believe you will not understand either. For I did not come to do my will but that of the one who sent me, and the will was him to be given over all who believe.
pass_b_english: For they did not attempt the perfect itself in faith but in unbelief, not having known the scriptures, which the prophets were announcing. For "unless you believe you will not understand either." (Isaiah 7:9) "For I did not come to do my will but the will of the one who sent me," (John 6:38) and the will was that he be given for all who believe (John 5:30) (Matthew 22:29).
source_text: Οὐ γὰρ ἐν πίστει αὐτὸ τὸ τέλειον ἐπεχείρησαν ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀπιστίᾳ, οὐκ ἐγνωκότες τὰς γραφάς, ἃς οἱ προφῆται ἤγγελον· τὸ γὰρ "ἐὰν μὴ πιστεύσητε οὐδ’ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε". "Οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον ποιῆσαι τὸ ἐμὸν θέλημα ἀλλὰ τὸ τοῦ πέμψαντός με", τὸ δὲ θέλημα ἦν τὸ δοθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων.
